Washington is coming off a 20-13 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, while the Giants are coming off a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Commanders are averaging 21.5 points per game with a points-per-game differential of -3.75. The Giants have fared a little better, averaging 22.8 points per game with a 1.25-point-per-game differential. Just one of their wins (Week 4 vs. Arizona) has been by 10 points or more, which means the Giants have squeaked by so far. The good news for the Giants is their defense has been dominant. New York has allowed just 172 points to opponents this season, the seventh-lowest mark in the league, making a valid argument that the defense has carried the team for most of the season. What will this week bring? Let’s take a look. Another Divisional Win? Please. The Giants have not beaten Washington since 2023. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants and Commanders, of course, tied in their meeting earlier this year. Before that, the last time the Giants beat Washington was November 19, 2023. So they are long overdue. With a win, the Giants would improve to 3-0-1 in the division and remain a couple of steps ahead of the Dallas Cowboys, who seem hot on their heels in the NFC East race. So yes, a lot is at stake for the Giants, who are 1-6 in games played on Thursday night since 2020. The Giants are aiming for their second straight win on Thursday Night Football . New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen has been working the phones to try to get John Harbaugh additional reinforcements. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. The Giants have been heavily linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Still, as of Sunday, Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that New York withdrew its offer after the Colts said they wanted much more for their lead back. That doesn’t mean that things can’t change, but it’s hard to see a deal happening, considering the Giants don’t have a 2027 fourth- or fifth-round pick to include in a trade, which appears to be a requisite to get a deal done. Given that the Colts also reportedly want a second-round pick, it’s hard to envision the Giants caving, especially after head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the team isn’t one player away. And then there is the other side of the coin, which is defensive tackle. The Giants really haven’t been strongly linked to any defensive tackles, at least not in the way they’ve been linked to Taylor. Could a surprise move be coming? McCarthy (hip), receiver Malik Nabers (knee), outside linebacker Abdul Carter (knee/back), and tackles Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are all on this week’s report. Harbaugh, in fact, expressed optimism that Skattebo and McCarthy, whose injuries appear to be the most significant, will be available for Thursday night. picks.blurb: Commanders vs. Giants bold predictions for Week 10 Thursday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL trade deadline grades Latest CFP rankings Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers NFL trade deadline tracker Colts keep Taylor Commanders vs. Giants bold predictions for Week 10 Thursday Night Football Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 10, 2026 at 9:05 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's two different stories as the Washington Commanders suffered another frustrating loss, while the New York Giants are thinking about big trade plans. But these teams meet on Thursday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the Week 10 contest. Carrying a record of 5-2-1, the Giants have eyes on the NFC East division title. They currently have a three-game lead over the Cowboys and won their only head-to-head matchup so far. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 2-5-1 and have failed miserably in late-game situations. Of course, this matchup will bring back memories of the Commanders' incredible gaffe. They had a chance to kick a game-winning field goal in overtime against the Giants, but ran a play and failed to spike the ball in time to stop the clock. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Giants QB JJ McCarthy will throw two TD passes It hasn't been a grand start for McCarthy with the Giants. In two starts, he has thrown for 379 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions. However, the completion percentages have been good at 71.4 and 63.2. And zero interceptions matter. McCarthy got harassed for eight sacks over the last two weeks. That's something that can't continue if the Giants want him to be successful. However, the Commanders have only 17 sacks this season. That's tied for No. 21 in the NFL. They've been a little better at pressure rate, with 12% ranking No. 15 in the league, according to statrankings.com. McCarty suffered an injury in Week 9, but is expected to play against the Commanders. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said McCarthy is making progress with the injury, according to the New York Post. "He's doing well,'' Harbaugh said. "We'll find out more during the course of the day and in a couple of days, but it does look like he's gonna play. We feel fairly good about that but don't want to get out over my skis with it, but it seems good so far.'' If the Giants are going to beat the Commanders, McCarthy will need to play well. And those two touchdown passes probably need to happen. The Commanders are tough against the run, allowing 102.3 yards per game to rank No. 12. Giants WR Malik Nabers will get 75-plus yards and a score It's squeaky-wheel production time for Nabers. He complained about his target share, so look for the Giants to feed him a little more this week. Nabers also fumed about being called out by Fox analyst Greg Olsen, according to his Instagram post via ESPN. "Yall be trying [to] create a narrative on me soo bad, it's actually crazy," Nabers wrote. "If you [don't] like the way I play the game, keep the camera off me!! SIMPLE!" "But [Olsen] calling me a bad teammate when every team I've been on, there's NOBODY I've played with has said dat bout me is crazy! My face the same way if I'm having a good game, bad, winning, or losing. If it's a problem: 1. Keep the camera off of me. 2. Pray bout it! Simple." Nabers is primed to have a big game. And look for the Giants to focus on helping him get it. Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will have 250-plus total yards The Commanders have little more than a Hail Mary chance of winning the division. For Dan Quinn: a Hail Mary is when the team with the ball throws it into the end zone on the game's final play. In other words, desperate times, but give it your best effort. You, too, Daniels. Although he tried to explain his lack of understanding against the Rams, according to NFL.com. "Last (moments) of the game … (the Rams) want to get the ball out of the quarterback's hand as fast as possible, so you know you have to take a shot at the end zone," Daniels said of his team's first attempt with eight seconds left. "So, if they could get home before you get the ball up, or you let your guys get down there, that's probably ideal." As for the last play? "It was the play call," Daniels said. "You got to execute it." But Daniels will show a little something against the Giants. Look for him to keep the team within shouting distance. If it comes down to the final play? Well, time will tell if Daniels and Quinn have learned anything at all this season. Game prediction: Giants 20, Commanders 17 It should be a tight contest. The Commanders seem to find ways to lose. away.blurb: The Commanders receiver corps is being thinned out by injury. Washington will play Sunday’s game against the L.A. Rams without Treylon Burks or Dyami Brown, the team announced Friday evening on its official injury report. Burks is dealing with a foot injury that kept him out of practice all week. Brown suffered a calf injury in Thursday’s practice that the Commanders are concerned about. Johnny Newton was considered questionable on the injury report, as those on IR with open practice windows usually are. We should learn about his availability on Saturday. TE John Bates – Limited all week with a shoulder injury All this comes shortly after Terry McLaurin was lost for the year with a torn petellar tendon in his knee. As The Athletic’s Nicki Jhabvala originally pointed, Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams were the only receivers at practice who have caught a pass in a game to this point. That’s, well, not great. The injury report was relatively clean outside of that, though the team has absorbed significant recent losses of those — like Javon Kinlaw and Jeremy McNichols — who are now on injured reserve. Also, NFL Network reports that superstar Rams edge rusher Myles Garrett is expected to be activated off injured reserve for Sunday’s game. away.headline: Commanders-Rams final injury report rules out two receivers, leaves McDuffie questionable
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders released their final injury report Friday ahead of their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. The report listed two of Washington's receivers, Treylon Burks (foot) and Dyami Brown (calf), as officially OUT against the Rams. Burks missed practice all week with an injured foot that he's been dealing with since the 49ers game, while Brown was added to Thursday's report as limited before missing Friday's practice. With Terry McLaurin already out for the season, Washington will need more from Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, who led the team with seven targets and five catches for 54 yards against Philadelphia . Van Jefferson could see more work, and Luke McCaffrey is another option. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spoke Friday about Jefferson's readiness: "I liked his approach. I liked his readiness, and so when called upon, I'd expect he'd play well." Rookie Jaden Bradley could also be elevated from the practice squad, although Washington hasn't announced that move. Elsewhere on the report, Jer'Zhan Newton is questionable with his pectoral injury despite practicing fully all three days. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window and must be activated from injured reserve before he can play. That decision carries some weight with Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw now on IR . Shy Tuttle (shoulder) was limited all week but carries no game designation, while Sam Cosmi (knee) returned to full participation Friday. John Bates (shoulder) was limited throughout the week but has no game designation either. Los Angeles has some injury problems of its own, particularly in the secondary . Cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder) is out, while Trent McDuffie (back) is questionable after missing every practice this week. Former Commanders safety Kam Curl (foot) is also questionable after returning to limited practice Friday. The Rams could be short-handed in the secondary, although McDuffie's and Curl's availability won't be settled until closer to kickoff. The Rams also listed long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) as doubtful, with tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs), linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), and receiver Jordan Whittington (back) questionable. Quarterback Matthew Stafford practiced fully throughout the week, while head coach Sean McVay expects Myles Garrett to play Sunday, pending his activation from injured reserve. Tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) was ruled out after injuring his hamstring in Friday’s practice . away.headline: J.J. McCarthy Injured, Latest Updates on Giants QB Ahead of TNF vs. Commanders
away.blurb: He also slammed his helmet down and then went to the locker room, and the Giants announced he was questionable to return with a hip injury. However, he returned from the locker room and then reentered the game. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy made it clear on Tuesday that he will be able to play on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders after suffering a hip injury in Week 9. McCarthy's comments come after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday that the Giants were "confident" he would be able to play. McCarthy took a hard hit while running during a play in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. He went to the sidelines at first and attempted to test it with a throw but winced in pain while falling to a knee. New York, of course, already lost Jaxson Dart to injury this season. The Giants traded for McCarthy in part as a response to Dart's injury, and the Michigan product played well in his immediate game action for the NFC East team. He threw for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints and earned the start in the ensuing matchup against the Houston Texans. Despite being on the road against a Texans defense with a number of headline players, McCarthy led the Giants to an overtime victory by throwing for 252 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. There was little question after that performance he would be the starter for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, although it did not go as well for him even before the injury. New York managed just two field goals in the first half and trailed by two points at intermission despite its own defense playing well against the Eagles. Jameis Winston, who was the quarterback the Giants initially turned to in the aftermath of Dart's injury, entered the game after McCarthy's injury and threw a touchdown to take the lead. While McCarthy returned, Winston will likely also be the signal-caller the team relies on in the future if McCarthy has any future issues.

New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

McCarthy was able to get to the sideline but appeared to be in a lot of pain. home.headline: J.J. McCarthy Injured, Latest Updates on Giants QB Ahead of TNF vs. Commanders
home.blurb: He also slammed his helmet down and then went to the locker room, and the Giants announced he was questionable to return with a hip injury. However, he returned from the locker room and then reentered the game. New York Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy made it clear on Tuesday that he will be able to play on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders after suffering a hip injury in Week 9. McCarthy's comments come after ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday that the Giants were "confident" he would be able to play. McCarthy took a hard hit while running during a play in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. He went to the sidelines at first and attempted to test it with a throw but winced in pain while falling to a knee. New York, of course, already lost Jaxson Dart to injury this season. The Giants traded for McCarthy in part as a response to Dart's injury, and the Michigan product played well in his immediate game action for the NFC East team. He threw for 243 yards, one touchdown and one interception during the fourth quarter of a game against the New Orleans Saints and earned the start in the ensuing matchup against the Houston Texans. Despite being on the road against a Texans defense with a number of headline players, McCarthy led the Giants to an overtime victory by throwing for 252 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. There was little question after that performance he would be the starter for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles, although it did not go as well for him even before the injury. New York managed just two field goals in the first half and trailed by two points at intermission despite its own defense playing well against the Eagles. Jameis Winston, who was the quarterback the Giants initially turned to in the aftermath of Dart's injury, entered the game after McCarthy's injury and threw a touchdown to take the lead. While McCarthy returned, Winston will likely also be the signal-caller the team relies on in the future if McCarthy has any future issues.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights John Breech predicts every Week 10 game, including a Lions victory over the Patriots in Munich Imagn Images I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks. I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place. I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell. Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere. Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games. The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out. Alright, now let's get to the picks for real NFL Week 10 picks Commanders (2-5-1) at Giants (5-2-1) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET (Amazon Prime) Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation. For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did. The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0 Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost. Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works. With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds. So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team. To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders. PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants Patriots (5-4) vs. Lions (6-2) in Munich Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (NFL Network) With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell? With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first. I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me. What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes. The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever. All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year. The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams. The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over. PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots Texans (3-5) at Browns (5-4) Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox) Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge on him or he's trying to get revenge on the Texans. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, there might not be any revenge involved at all here. Since trading Watson to the Browns in March 2022, the Texans have made the playoffs three times, and they've won their division twice. On the other hand, Watson has been injured for the majority of his time in Cleveland; he's won just 14 games since 2022, and the Browns have paid him roughly $14.5 million per win. If Tom Brady had earned $14.5 million per win, he would have made over $3 billion in his career. Do you know how many Hofbrauhaus beers you could buy with that money? The worst part for the Browns is that they're still in QB purgatory, which is basically where they've been since returning to the NFL in 1999. Although Watson is playing well this year, especially late in games, I'm not sure that's a good thing. If he somehow leads Cleveland to the playoffs, the Browns might actually talk themselves into re-signing him, which doesn't seem like a great idea. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It's been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it'll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots' 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers' worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: "Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven't turned the ball over, they haven't exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it's just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven't quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error." The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

The Patriots traded a 2028 first-round pick to acquire Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason, but the results have been underwhelming through the first half of the season. The Los Angeles Rams were also interested in trading for Brown during the offseason, but they were reportedly scared off by the medical concerns with his knee, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported. Brown has only caught passes in each of the three games he played in this season, bringing his tally up to nine receptions for 101 yards and no touchdowns. There was belief that the eight-year veteran would be a great fit as a vertical threat for quarterback Drake Maye, who has been one of the best deep-ball passers in the league. home.headline: Detroit Lions Player Says He Doesn't Yet Have Full Movement In His Body After Terrifying Injury
home.blurb: “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the team shared. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.” By Carly Ledbetter Senior Reporter, HuffPost LOADING ERROR LOADING Detroit Lions player Jack Campbell has issued his first statement on his condition, just days after enduring a terrifying neck injury in a game against the Vikings. Campbell, 26, did not appear to be moving while he was taken off the field, as his teammates looked on with tears and concern. Campbell said Wednesday he is still working on regaining movement in his body, though he does have full movement in his lower body at this time. “I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body,” he said in a statement. “I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. My faith in God has never been stronger.” Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions lays on the ground after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings on Nov. 1. Mike Mulholland via Getty Images “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” he added. “I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you.” Dan Campbell, head coach for the Detroit Lions, previously spoke about visiting Campbell in the hospital, though he declined to share the specifics of his injury or his progress. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said during a press conference on Monday. “Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. It’s about the recovery, and it’s a small setback.” Both Lions and Vikings players took a knee on the turf as Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell (not pictured) received medical treatment. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Advertisement The Lions also kept details about Campbell’s injury vague in a statement shared on Monday. Campbell and his wife, Megan, recently welcomed a 4-month-old son named Cooper. home.headline: Lions LB Jack Campbell 'determined' to play football again: Live updates, injury news
home.blurb: Aidan Hutchinson told CBS Sports' Melanie Collins that it wasn't hard to get motivated this week, pointing out that it was weird without Jack Campbell in meetings. Campbell's medical diagnosis has not yet been made public. Medical experts reached by USA TODAY did point out the uniqueness of Campbell's post-injury symptoms, saying that delayed recovery of upper-body movement could be associated with central cord syndrome . It's a rare medical condition common in people with spinal injuries who have fallen forward and land on their forehead and extend backward, similar to the action exhibited by Campbell’s head and neck at impact. A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 and received the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football. Campbell slid right in as a key piece of the Lions' defense after arriving in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season. The Detroit Lions took the field in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins without a key member of their defense – Jack Campbell. It marked the Lions' first contest since the linebacker suffered a terrifying neck injury during the team's Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings . The injury left Campbell laying on the field motionless before being carted off the field on a backboard as emotional teammates looked on . Campbell issued a statement about his condition on Wednesday, Nov. 4. He said that he has movement in his lower body and was making progress towards regaining movement in his upper body. It was an encouraging update that extended beyond the generic ones provided earlier in the week . From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. The Lions escaped Miami with a 19-9 win over the Dolphins, but it was clear that Jack Campbell was still top of mind. "A lot of what we said was win No. 6 for 46," Dan Campbell told reporters . "And we did that today. We got that done." EXCLUSIVE: Rare diagnosis could explain Lions LB Jack Campbell's neck injury update, spine experts say On Nov. 7, the Lions announced they were placing the linebacker on injured reserve. It's a reminder that Campbell has a long way to go in his recovery, but he remains determined to get back on the field, according to CBS Sports' Melanie Collins. "He is determined to get back on this football field, telling Dan Campbell: 'Just make sure the house is taken care of until I can get back,'" Collins reported on the CBS broadcast of the game. Mahomes didn't end up missing an offensive play in the Chiefs' win, but he did reveal after the game that he'd need further testing on his elbow. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, those tests did not reveal a major injury and Mahomes is expected to be good to go for Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. away.headline: Report: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes avoids major elbow injury
away.blurb: "Patrick took a pretty good shot to the throwing arm today and came off the field in some pain. We checked him out right away and he told us his elbow was sore, but he was determined to get back out there," Reid said. "He returned, made some throws, and kept competing the way he always does. He's one of the toughest players I've ever coached, and he doesn't like missing snaps." Nov 09 (Field Level Media) - Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes avoided a major injury to his right elbow, according to a media report Sunday night. An MRI exam revealed an elbow strain or sprain but no significant damage, NFL Network reported. Mahomes will be monitored for pain and swelling over the next few days, leaving his status uncertain for next Sunday's game against the host Atlanta Falcons. Mahomes injured his throwing arm during Kansas City's 35-12 victory over the New York Jets. He completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns but said afterward that his arm did not feel right early in the second half. "From the stories you hear, whenever you can grab the ball and try to throw it, you can't throw," Mahomes said. "Once I threw the football, I knew it wasn't -- hopefully, I haven't done the test yet -- it wasn't ligament-type stuff, it was more muscle-type stuff." Mahomes was drilled by Jets rookie edge rusher David Bailey while raring back to fire a pass downfield with 1:33 left in the first half. He came off the field supporting his right elbow with his left arm and appeared to be in significant pain. Head coach Andy Reid said the Chiefs would follow all of the proper steps to confirm Mahomes is not hurt. If upcoming tests give the Chiefs pause, Reid said the plan will be to "prepare Justin (Fields)" to face the Falcons on Sunday. Fields did not attempt a pass Sunday but ran twice for minus-1 yard. Mahomes returned to start Week 1 after sustaining a season-ending left knee injury in 2025.

The Kansas City Chiefs have taken advantage of the Indianapolis Colts' ongoing roster teardown by bolstering their receiving corps. The Colts traded wideout Josh Downs to the Chiefs Tuesday in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks, according to The Ringer and Netflix's Tom Pelissero . Chiefs' Fantasy Outlook 😮‍💨 Downs is playing this season under a $4.2 million cap hit on his expiring rookie contract. The 25-year-old wideout requested a trade from the Colts ahead of Week 8, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . The Colts, which were 2-5 at the time, had already made their deadline position clear by trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. Indianapolis has since also traded Keenan Allen as part of the team's ongoing roster teardown. Downs has served as the team's slot receiver amid the heel injury that has sidelined Alec Pierce for most of the season. While dealing with extra attention from opposing defenses in Pierce's absence, Downs recorded 33 catches for 354 yards and a touchdown in nine games prior to his trade. The fourth-year wideout will hope leaving Indianapolis for a wide receiver room led by Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy will give him an opportunity to increase his production down the stretch of the season. The biggest question for the Colts will now be what direction the franchise should take after dismissing former general manager Chris Ballard before reportedly turning down offers for Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor ahead of the deadline. The Chiefs were looking to add wide receiver depth at the deadline after losing Rice and Tyquan Thornton to injury early in the season. away.headline: Chiefs HC Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes injury update ahead of Falcons game
away.blurb: The Chiefs’ quarterback went to the sideline to get checked out and worked on. He was back on the field for the second half and helped lead his team to victory while playing through pain, but he later underwent further evaluations, including an MRI. Ian Rapoport reported on NFL Network that Mahomes’ MRI “did not reveal significant damage,” and he was diagnosed with an elbow strain/sprain. Rapoport said he expected the Chiefs quarterback would be monitored and possibly limited at practices. The Kansas City Chiefs ‘ 35-12 win over the New York Jets didn’t come without some concerns about star quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who suffered an injury before halftime. Mahomes was hit by the Jets’ David Bailey on a strip-sack late in the second quarter. Edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr. also hit Mahomes on the play. He then came up grimacing in pain and holding his right throwing elbow, raising immediate worries about his condition. According to ESPN , Chiefs head coach Andy Reid spoke to reporters Monday and indicated that Mahomes was “day-to-day” with his elbow injury. Reid also said Mahomes was at the training facility that morning for treatment on the injury. More news: Tom Brady Throws Subtle Shade at Patriots QB Drake Maye After Packers Loss In Sunday’s game, he threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both of which went to running back Kenneth Walker III. However, Mahomes’ situation heading into the next game is still uncertain. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of [him getting] some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We’ll just see where it goes from there. He’s in good spirits,” Reid said, also adding he was glad they weren’t practicing today and that they would see where Mahomes was at Wednesday. He’ll reportedly continue to receive treatment as they attempt to reduce swelling in the injured elbow. The Chiefs have three practices this week, but Reid was uncertain whether Mahomes would fully participate due to his injury. Waiting in the wings for a potential start is Justin Fields, whom the team acquired this past March in a trade with the Jets. That may not be the most encouraging news after his brief performance in Sunday’s game. Fields played in the matchup against his former team, recording two rushing attempts for negative yardage and losing a fumble on a first-quarter quarterback sneak attempt. While Fields is nowhere near the type of quarterback Mahomes is, he might give Kansas City a suitable replacement on the field against their next opponent. home.headline: Chiefs HC Andy Reid reveals Patrick Mahomes injury update ahead of Falcons game
home.blurb: The Chiefs’ quarterback went to the sideline to get checked out and worked on. He was back on the field for the second half and helped lead his team to victory while playing through pain, but he later underwent further evaluations, including an MRI. Ian Rapoport reported on NFL Network that Mahomes’ MRI “did not reveal significant damage,” and he was diagnosed with an elbow strain/sprain. Rapoport said he expected the Chiefs quarterback would be monitored and possibly limited at practices. The Kansas City Chiefs ‘ 35-12 win over the New York Jets didn’t come without some concerns about star quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who suffered an injury before halftime. Mahomes was hit by the Jets’ David Bailey on a strip-sack late in the second quarter. Edge rusher Will McDonald IV and defensive lineman Darrell Jackson Jr. also hit Mahomes on the play. He then came up grimacing in pain and holding his right throwing elbow, raising immediate worries about his condition. According to ESPN , Chiefs head coach Andy Reid spoke to reporters Monday and indicated that Mahomes was “day-to-day” with his elbow injury. Reid also said Mahomes was at the training facility that morning for treatment on the injury. More news: Tom Brady Throws Subtle Shade at Patriots QB Drake Maye After Packers Loss In Sunday’s game, he threw for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both of which went to running back Kenneth Walker III. However, Mahomes’ situation heading into the next game is still uncertain. “It was more positive news than negative news on Patrick. It looks like it’s just a matter of [him getting] some rehabbing in there and getting rid of some of the soreness. We’ll just see where it goes from there. He’s in good spirits,” Reid said, also adding he was glad they weren’t practicing today and that they would see where Mahomes was at Wednesday. He’ll reportedly continue to receive treatment as they attempt to reduce swelling in the injured elbow. The Chiefs have three practices this week, but Reid was uncertain whether Mahomes would fully participate due to his injury. Waiting in the wings for a potential start is Justin Fields, whom the team acquired this past March in a trade with the Jets. That may not be the most encouraging news after his brief performance in Sunday’s game. Fields played in the matchup against his former team, recording two rushing attempts for negative yardage and losing a fumble on a first-quarter quarterback sneak attempt. While Fields is nowhere near the type of quarterback Mahomes is, he might give Kansas City a suitable replacement on the field against their next opponent. Kansas City’s next game is on the road against the Atlanta Falcons, a team that lost their last two games and, at 3-6, is last in the NFC South. Meanwhile, the Chiefs improved to 6-2 yesterday and are just below the 7-2 Denver Broncos in the AFC West. Mahomes suffered a painful injury to his throwing elbow during the 35-12 triumph at Arrowhead Stadium, briefly raising fears that Kansas City could lose its franchise quarterback at a crucial stage of the season. However, the Chiefs coach confirmed that Mahomes remains day to day, leaving his participation in this week's practices uncertain. The concerning incident occurred late in the second quarter when Jets rookie defensive end David Bailey struck Mahomes ' right arm as he attempted to release a pass. The collision forced a fumble and left the quarterback clutching his elbow on the ground before Kansas City's medical staff examined him. Mahomes subsequently tested his throwing motion on the sideline and returned to action without missing an offensive snap, eventually completing 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns. An MRI conducted after the game reportedly revealed no major structural damage, providing further encouragement following an incident that initially appeared considerably more serious. Mahomes acknowledged the frightening nature of the collision but explained that he was determined to continue once the discomfort became manageable. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Houston Texans (3-5) head to Cleveland on Sunday looking to continue a dramatic midseason turnaround when they face the Browns (5-4) at Huntington Bank Field. The Texans opened the season with four straight losses but have won three of their last four. The division may be out of reach as the Jaguars lead the Texans by three games in the AFC South but Houston is back in the race for a Wild Card spot. Cleveland takes the field after dropping their last two games which has dropped them out of first in the AFC North and 1.5 games behind the Steelers and the Bengals. Houston is coming off its most explosive performance of the season, a 44-22 road rout of the winless Los Angeles Chargers. C.J. Stroud played through an illness and completed 21 of 35 passes for 384 yards, five touchdowns and one interception. He connected with four different players for scores, including 63-yard touchdowns to Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte , with Boutte finishing with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. The Texans led 24-9 at halftime, stretched the advantage to 38-9 early in the fourth quarter and defensively overwhelmed Justin Herbert , sacking him eight times. Cleveland arrives home following a gut-wrenching 23-22 overtime loss at New Orleans. With Deshaun Watson sidelined by a concussion, Shedeur Sanders started and finished 19-of-31 for 297 yards and two touchdowns, including a 64-yard go-ahead strike to KC Concepcion late in the fourth quarter. After New Orleans regained the lead, Andre Szmyt’s 51-yard field goal forced overtime. The Saints scored first in the extra period, but Sanders answered by finding Harold Fannin Jr. for a 39-yard touchdown before Cleveland went for two and the win; the conversion failed, dropping the Browns to 5-4. The matchup also renews a surprisingly balanced series. Houston leads the all-time matchup 8-7, including the postseason, but Cleveland won four consecutive meetings from 2020 through the 2023 regular season. Their most recent clash reversed that trend in emphatic fashion: in the 2023 AFC Wild Card round, Stroud threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns as Houston demolished Cleveland 45-14, with the Texans turning two Joe Flacco interceptions into defensive touchdowns. In addition to Watson’s health, other storylines include the Texans’ pass rush against Cleveland’s quarterback protection particularly after Sanders was sacked five times in New Orleans and Houston just recorded eight sacks against the Chargers. Let’s dive further into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. home.headline: Saints rookie WR Jordyn Tyson plans to make debut vs. Browns after missing first 7 games with hamstring injury: report
home.blurb: Saints head coach Kellen Moore told reporters that Tyson’s foot slipped out from under him as he was hit from behind. Moore clarified that the issue wasn’t related to the receiver’s injury track record. “Any player in that situation probably has the same diagnosis coming out of this.” Tyson began his college career at Colorado, where he teased his tantalizing potential by averaging 21.4 yards per reception and housing a punt return as a freshman in 2022. In 2024, Tyson broke out with the Sun Devils, helping them reach the College Football Playoff and finished with 75 catches, 1,101 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. Even during a shortened 2025 campaign, he totaled nine TDs, with one of them arriving on the ground. The delayed debut of New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is reportedly right around the corner. Tyson, this year’s No. 8 overall pick who missed the Saints’ first seven games with a right hamstring injury, plans to play Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . The former Arizona State standout “should be good to go,” Schultz reported Saturday. Tyson’s latest hamstring setback occurred in August during a training camp practice. He left that joint session with the Jacksonville Jaguars early once his run after the catch ended with an awkward fall near the sideline . “I think my understanding of this one, any player that was put in his situation where your foot slips and you get shoved from behind, this has nothing to do with Jordyn's history,” Moore said at the time, per ESPN . Notably, Tyson missed four games last season at Arizona State with multiple hamstring problems, and his injury obstacles affected his pre-draft process. Still, the Saints selected him in the top 10 . Funny enough, that special teams score came against his future school, Arizona State, on a day when he also reeled in five passes for 115 yards and another TD. Staying on the field has been a challenge for the 6-foot-2, 203-pound Tyson. Down the stretch of his lone go-around at Colorado, he suffered a torn ACL, MCL and PCL. He missed the end of a memorable 2024 season with the Sun Devils due to a broken collarbone that sidelined him for the Big 12 title game and the CFP. But he’s thought to have WR1 upside, given his ball skills — including his knack for making contested catches — and his ability to play every receiver spot on the field with impressive quickness. At the moment, the 2-5 Saints are tied for third in the league with 39 pass attempts per game . Without a reliable run game, Tyler Shough is having to chuck the ball around the yard. Having Tyson at his disposal should help.

home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. The Vikings have dropped two games in a row to fall into third place in the NFC North, and it appears that Murray may miss more than just Week 9. The former No. 1 overall pick was diagnosed with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, putting his status in question for the team's Week 10 matchup with the Green Bay Packers. Pelissero: Kyler Murray was diagnosed with a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline, the Vikings may look to add a quarterback after Carson Wentz was so bad against Buffalo that he was benched late in the game for Max Brosmer. The Vikings are just 31st in the NFL in EPA/Play on offense and 30th in success rate despite a 6-2 start. Murray's injury has shifted the odds for the Vikings vs. Packers matchup in Week 10, and it appears that he's facing an uphill battle to play. He hasn't been great, but the former top pick certainly gives this team a better chance the win than Wentz, who turned the ball over three times and failed to lead a touchdown drive in Week 9. Max Brosmer is the only other quarterback on the Vikings' roster, and the team may be regretting the J.J. McCarthy trade at this point in the season. It's possible Minnesota could target a veteran quarterback like Kirk Cousins or Daniel Jones at the deadline, but neither of those players is a massive upgrade from Murray. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Opening lines for Week 10 matchup | Daily Norseman Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Minnesota Vikings Community Daily Norseman November 11, 2026 Daily Norseman Notifications Notifications Sections News By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds Minnesota Vikings Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand News By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Minnesota Vikings Odds Totally unsurprising, to say the least After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. The Commanders needed a touchdown to force overtime or take the lead against the Rams and had mere seconds to obtain it when they made two questionable calls. With eight seconds to play in a 20-13 game, quarterback Jayden Daniels took a deep shot and left the ball short of the goal line. That would have been a reasonable throw if the Commanders had any timeouts at their disposal, but they were out of them at that point of the fourth quarter. A completion in that spot would have ended the game. Then, on the final play of the afternoon, Washington dialed up a hook-and-ladder play instead of a Hail Mary, which came up well shy of the end zone. Rather than having Daniels chuck the ball 31 yards, they looked for something underneath that was not there. Coach Dan Quinn and offensive coordinator David Blough have drawn significant scrutiny, and those end-of-game decisions will not pull them out from under the microscope. It would be a steep drop for Cousins to go from a potential trade piece and starter for a contending team to a second-string quarterback, but if the offense flounders in the weeks to come and the Raiders slip out of the postseason hunt, coach Klint Kubiak could hand the keys to the offense to Fernando Mendoza . The No. 1 overall pick will likely get a look as the starter before the season is done. Any further struggles from Cousins may expedite that. Shedeur Sanders ' terrific individual effort came with the caveat that it did not result in a win. The Cleveland Browns quarterback showed the makings of a viable starter in the 23-22 overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints , though. That is a development that gives the Browns some flexibility moving forward if Deshaun Watson falters upon his return from the concussion protocol. And it could even lead to an internal quarterback controversy if any of the Browns decision-makers view Sanders' 297-yard, two-touchdown performance as a successful audition for the job. Green Bay also ruled out five: linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), guard/tackle Travis Glover (knee), center Sean Rhyan (ankle), tight end Josh Whyle (concussion) and edge rusher Micah Parsons (knee). Both Nixon and Lloyd popped up on the injury report during the practice week. Nixon didn't practice Thursday but returned in limited fashion Friday. He's played in 76 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. "It's always concerning when a guy doesn't practice on a Thursday but, if I know Kei like I think I do, I would expect him to put himself in a position to potentially go out there and play," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur on Friday morning. While Rhyan was ruled out, LaFleur told reporters on Thursday that he doesn't anticipate Green Bay's starting center going on IR. Rhyan hasn't practiced since injuring his ankle four snaps into the Packers' Week 7 game in Detroit. Receiver Christian Watson (ribs), guard Aaron Banks (knee) and safety Javon Bullard (personal) didn't receive game statuses and will be available Sunday. Watson broke a rib during the Packers' 27-19 win over Carolina but returned to finish the game. He wore protective padding while practicing in a limited capacity this week. away.headline: Report: Cardinals signing Jaguars' QB to active roster
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are signing QB Joey Aguilar off the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad and onto their active roster, according to Jeremy Fowler. This addition at quarterback for the Cardinals comes after the team traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens and with Gardner Minshew "likely" needing season-ending surgery on a torn UCL, per Adam Schefter . Already on the roster at quarterback for the Cardinals are Carson Beck and Josh Johnson, whom Arizona signed off the Bengals ' practice squad on Monday. Aguilar signed with the Jaguars following the 2026 NFL draft as an undrafted rookie. He appeared in all three preseason games, completing 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards with a touchdown pass. After being released during roster cutdowns, the Jaguars brought Aguilar back on the practice squad. Throughout offseason programs and training camp, Liam Coen liked what he saw from Aguilar and wanted to continue working with him. On the 53-man roster at QB for the Jaguars are Trevor Lawrence and Quinn Ewers. Nick Mullens remains on the practice squad. This article originally appeared on Jaguars Wire: Report: Cardinals signing Jaguars' QB to active roster

away.headline: Jaguars-Ravens Injury Report: Why Recent History Doesn't Bode Well for Bhayshul Tuten
away.blurb: The Jaguars released their final injury report for Thursday's Week 9 battle with the Baltimore Ravens, and it featured two big names as questionable: running back Bhayshul Tuten and defensive end Travon Walker. There is understandable concern for both, with Walker limited in practice on Tuesday and Wednesday after sustaining a rib injury in last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts. But recent history under this Jaguars regime suggests Walker has at least a chance to play. It does not say the same about Tuten. Simply put, the Jaguars will more than likely need Chris Rodriguez Jr. to step into a starting role on Thursday based on how they have handled past injury situations. Tuten did not practice on Tuesday or Wednesday, despite Jaguars head coach Liam Coen indicating in his pre-practice press conference that Tuten would have some sort of practice activity. Instead, Tuten was a DNP for the second day in a row, which has resulted in a missed game each time during the Coen era. This is the 25th game where the Jaguars are led by Coen and his staff. In the previous 24 final injury reports, the Jaguars have had 27 instances where a player did not practice during the week. In all 27 of those instances, the player missed the game that week. The key difference here is that Tuten is at least listed as questionable. All 27 previous instances of players missing practice led to them being outright ruled out, which of course has not been the case with Tuten. Coen has already tabbed Tuten as a game-time decision, something he has done two other times this year: in Week 1 with Cole Van Lanen and LeQuint Allen, who were each listed as questionable but played. The difference is that Van Lanen and Allen at least practiced that week. If this was a full week and not a Thursday Night Game, which the Jaguars have not played under Coen before, perhaps things would be different. But for now, most signs point toward Tuten not being available just simply based on the Jaguars' history under Coen. Perhaps one key that could answer the Tuten question is how Coen approached Van Lanen's status in Week 1. Van Lanen was coming off a serious knee injury that had kept him out of the entirety of training camp, though he returned in time to be limited in practice in Week 1. But a few weeks before then, here is what Coen had to say. away.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter Shares Bhayshul Tuten Injury Update For Jaguars
away.blurb: The second-year RB was injured on Sunday, although he finished out that game before it became apparently clear that the injury was worse than thought. On the Jaguars' injury report, Tuten is listed as questionable — and it's a key question. There may not be a full update until the inactive report at 6:50 p.m. ET, but in the meantime, there are little hints out there, including from ESPN's NFL insider, Adam Schefter. The Ravens are starting Joe Fagnano at quarterback, so it might not matter — but Jacksonville would still feel more secure if Tuten was available. ESPN's Adam Schefter Shares Bhayshul Tuten Injury Update For Jaguars Unlock the latest Heavy on Jaguars news — direct to your inbox. The Jacksonville Jaguars have a big injury question mark for Thursday Night Football: Bhayshul Tuten. Tuten didn't practice at all in the short week before the Jags face the Baltimore Ravens to open Week 9. If Tuten doesn't play, a key contributor is removed from the Jaguars' offense. If he does play, will Tuten be at full strength? That's certainly a reasonable thing to wonder, too. Adam Schefter on Bhayshul Tuten Schefter appeared on the 9 a.m. hour of SportsCenter on ESPN2 on Thursday morning and spoke about a number of topics, including briefly about Tuten. The insider said that Tuten is expected to go through warmups before the game for a final assessment, and Schefter said it “wouldn't surprise me” if Tuten ended up active for the game. That's more speculative than fact, and it does sound like the warmups are going to matter. But it's also a bit of a positive outlook for Jaguars fans (and fantasy football managers) who are hoping for good news. What Happened to Bhayshul Tuten? Video circulated after the Jaguars' 42-7 win on Sunday over the Colts that Tuten had been hurt during the first quarter. On a running play, it was clear Tuten had rolled his foot and/or ankle, and it looked painful. Somehow, Tuten played the rest of the game (and had a great game). The Jags rested their starters a bit early with the big lead, which may have been helpful for Tuten in retrospect. Still, it seems the Jaguars may not have realized the extent of the injury until after the fact. Tuten didn't practice all week and is a legitimate question mark for Thursday. home.blurb: Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week how the coaching staff plans to prepare, if Campbell is out for the foreseeable future. "So, we may need a little bit of help. We're looking at everything. We'll adjust as we go. (Lions Executive Vice President and General Manager) Brad (Holmes) and I will get together here this afternoon, tomorrow and figure some of this out.” After visiting the Detroit Lions Allen Park Performance Center, a decision was made on former Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans linebacker Owen Pappoe. According to multiple reports, the 26-year-old will ink a deal to join Detroit's practice squad. Detroit's linebackers unit was in need of added depth this week after two players went down against the Minnesota Vikings with significant injuries. Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was lost for the remainder of the 2026 season due to a hamstring injury. Captain Jack Campbell is still hospitalized after a frightening neck injury suffered in the second half of a 19-15 Week 8 victory against a division rival. According to an Athletic scouting report , "The Tigers’ two-year captain ran the fastest combine 40 (4.39) among the linebackers. The 6-foot, 225-pounder isn’t particularly big, but was an effective leader/communicator in the middle of the Auburn defense who should benefit as a run-and-chase, weakside linebacker at the next level. Pappoe had a pair of 90-tackle seasons at Auburn." home.blurb: Bills acquire playmaking safety Amani Hooker from Titans, send second-round pick in return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL The Bills announced at Tuesday's NFL trade deadline that they are sending the Titans a 2027 second-round draft pick and will also receive a 2027 fifth-round selection in return to acquire Hooker. The Bills also inquired about eight-time Pro Bowl Cardinals safety Budda Baker before trading for Hooker, NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports . Tatum, Celtics rout Brown, Sixers Jason Owens Staff writer Tue, November 10, 2026 at 9:04 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads With their sights set on a Super Bowl title, the Buffalo Bills are adding a dynamic defensive playmaker in trading for Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker. The move bolsters a defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game. The Bills have one of the league's best offenses helmed by an MVP quarterback in Josh Allen, but their pass defense has been a liability throughout the season. Trading a second-round pick to acquire Hooker is a steep price, but the move addresses a clear area of need for a Super Bowl contender. Hooker, 28, is a difference-maker in the secondary. He joins the Bills tied for the league lead with five interceptions alongside six passes defended. The interception tally also ties a career high through just seven games. Hooker has 17 interceptions and 45 passes defended in his career. Hooker is also an accomplished defender against the run. He ranks second on the Titans this season with 52 total tackles. He projects to plug in as an immediate starter for the Bills. An eighth-year veteran, Hooker has played his entire NFL career for the Titans since they selected him in the fourth round of the 2019 draft. For the Titans, they part with a long-term veteran leader and one of their best players. But Hooker is best suited to contribute to a team ready to win now, and at 1-7, the Titans are not that. A second-round pick is a valuable asset as they seek to continue to rebuild around second-year quarterback Cam Ward.

Schefter reported the injury occurred on the first play of Miami's 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Sieler proceeded to log 50 more snaps on defense and special teams. The 31-year-old has been a stalwart along Miami's defensive front since first signing with the team midway through the 2019 season. He has appeared in 110 total games for the Dolphins. Report: Malik Willis Going on IR Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury As expected, this is a rebuilding year for Miami, which is tied for the NFL's second-worst record (1-7). Because of that, Sieler looked like a possible trade candidate prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET deadline. That option is obviously off the table now. If the Dolphins believe they can make a quick turnaround in 2027, they may continue to see Sieler as an important piece of the defense. General manager Jon-Eric Sullivan might instead view his three-year $64 million extension a little differently due to the injury. away.blurb: My bigger concern is Willis’ durability. He’s been on the injury report the past two weeks with a groin problem, meaning he’s now spent four of the nine weeks of the season on the injury report with groin, toe and right thumb ailments. Willis is a 6-foot-1, 225-pound quarterback, which isn’t big, and he takes extra hits when he runs so you worry about him remaining available over a full season. It’s a shame that defensive tackle Zach Sieler is out for the season with an injury that he sustained on the first play of last Sunday’s 19-9 loss to the Detroit Lions. Sieler is a key part of a run defense that is 16th against the run (111.8 yards allowed per game) so he’ll be missed on the field. away.headline: Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis to injured reserve
away.blurb: After he was aquired, McCord said of his strengths: "Knowing the call and then seeing what the defense plays and getting the ball to the right guy on time, allowing the playmakers to go out and make plays. And then my accuracy too, I think those two things really showed in the preseason and are probably a big reason why I'm here." Willis has played through injuries to a groin, a toe and a thumb. This is a core issue, according to reports. Willis will miss games at Indianapolis, at Buffalo, vs. the Jets and at Denver. Kyle McCord, whom Miami acquired in a trade from Packers before the season, is in line to start. Willis' ranks in the NFL are: 27th (passer rating), 26th (passing yards) and 25th (passing touchdowns). Despite some glimpses, Willis has not yet provided assurances that he is Miami's quarterback of the future. With a Top 3 NFL Draft pick on the horizon in April of 2027, quarterback will certainly be an option. Willis has a big arm and athleticism, when healthy. But he continues to work on decision-making, accuracy and timing. Willis, 27, agreed to a 3-year, $67 million contract with $45 million guaranteed. Miami would like Willis to at least be their starting quarterback for two seasons. But nothing in life is guaranteed, especially for NFL quarterbacks. McCord, 24, played at Ohio State and Syracuse and was a 6th round pick of the Eagles. On trading deadline day, the Dolphins did not make a deal. So Austin Jackson, Josh Uche and anyone else mentioned as intriguing trade candidates remain on the roster. Joe Schad is a journalist covering the Miami Dolphins and the NFL at The Palm Beach Post. The Jets are now 2-7 on the season. All playoff hopes have evaporated. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-21 record. We are reaching Kotite-ish levels of ineptitude. This week the Jets visited the Kansas City Chiefs. They kept it competitve for a half. In the first half the Jets outgained the Chiefs. They won the turnover battle. They had more than twice the time of possession as the Chiefs. They scored on four out of five possessions. The Chiefs scored only twice. And still the Jets trailed at halftime, 14 – 12. It was an ill omen. The second half was all Chiefs. They scored 21 unanswered points and cruised to a 35 – 12 blowout over the Jets. It was just one more humiliation in a decade filled with them. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-7 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets limp home to face the first place Buffalo Bills in East Rutherford, New Jersey next Sunday. The Bills have won three straight games and six of seven on the year. Josh Allen is playing like an MVP candidate, as usual. The Bills offense is humming, leading the NFL in points scored. The Bills defense has had some issues, but they held the Baltimore Ravens to 144 yards of offense and just 10 points last week. This will be a formidable challenge for a reeling Jets team just trying to stop the bleeding. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Bills will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets home underdogs by 8.5 points. The game has an over/under of 51.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Bills are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can keep the game competitive for a while as they did against the Chiefs for a half.
