Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Sam Darnold (quad, rib) and Drew Lock (oblique, elbow) are both banged up heading into Week 10, and there's no guarantee that either player will be good to go on Sunday. So, third-string quarterback Jalen Milroe could end up getting the start, and he's never attempted a pass in an NFL regular season game. According to Seahawks beat reporter Brady Henderson, Lock suffered an oblique injury in the win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, and his status for Week 10 is "up in the air." Mike Macdonald said Drew Lock suffered an oblique injury today and his status for this coming week is up in the air. That’s what Lock was getting examined in the medical tent. Macdonald didn’t have a great feel for whether Sam Darnold (quad/rib) can get back this week. Meanwhile, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Darnold is in jeopardy of missing Week 10 and that the team may want to hold him out through the Week 11 bye. “Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold, who already has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals with a quad injury and a cracked rib, also is in danger of missing Seattle's Week 10 game against the Raiders, league sources told ESPN,” Schefter wrote. “Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers. “Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday night's loss to the Bears, and played through a painful injury, before hurting his quad later in the game.” Darnold missed most of Week 1 and all of Week 2 with a glute injury, yet the Seahawks are now 3-0 when Lock plays in the 2026 seasn. The shift in the odds for this matchup came partially due to Lock's injury, as Milroe is somewhat of an unknown quantity at the NFL level. DraftKings Sportsbook had the Seahawks as 7.5-point road favorites in the lookahead line for this matchup prior to Week 9. However, even with the Seahawks winning to get back over .500, the odds shifted to Seattle -3 , a full 4.5-point swing. That's a sign that the betting market isn't sure about the Seahawks' quarterback situation, and it's possible this line could move further if Milroe ends up being named the starter. The Raiders (4-5) have not beaten any real contenders this season, but they are competent enough to hang around in a game with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. Since Seattle has a bye in Week 11, it may decide to rest Darnold so he's ready for the stretch run. After all, there is no guarantee that the Seahawks make the playoffs after winning just five of their first nine games. The odds for this game should move more once Seattle's practice report comes out on Wednesday. If both Lock and Darnold aren't able to participate, it would point toward Milroe getting a chance to play in Week 10. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. away.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. away.headline: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

The decision means Drew Lock is expected to make his second consecutive start, although he is also managing an oblique injury and an elbow issue. Seattle will travel to Las Vegas for the November 15 contest at Allegiant Stadium, with the Seahawks hoping to avoid another quarterback setback before their Week 11 bye. Darnold suffered a quadriceps injury late in Seattle's Week 8 game against the Chicago Bears. He also sustained a cracked rib during the contest, with Macdonald revealing that the quarterback had been playing through the injury. The Seahawks initially described his absence as week to week. home.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

So I think more than anything right now with the Rams, because this is going to be your number one receiver. Davante was playing great, but Davante was brought in to complement Puka Nacua based on all of the things that he did in this offense,” Spears said. away.headline: Rams EDGE Myles Garrett’s huge injury return is a Los Angeles first since Aaron Donald
away.blurb: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett made an immediate impact in his return, notching three sacks and forcing a fumble during Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. The performance put the 30-year-old in rare company, as he became the first player in franchise history to record three sacks and a forced fumble since star pass rusher Aaron Donald accomplished the feat back in 2020. His first sack came in the second quarter when he knocked the ball out of quarterback Jayden Daniels’ hands. Linebacker Omar Speights recovered the fumble, helping Los Angeles get into position for a field goal that reduced Washington’s advantage to 10-6 before halftime. Garrett added two more sacks in the fourth quarter, including one against Daniels after coming around left tackle Brandon Coleman. His final takedown turned out to be a game-changer, as he beat the replacement center with a quick move through the middle to prevent the Commanders from building momentum during their late comeback attempt. Garrett’s return helped Los Angeles improve to 5-4, extend its winning streak to three games and move above .500 for the first time this season. The Rams will next face the division-rival Arizona Cardinals before entering its Week 11 bye. Garrett, who underwent knee surgery in mid-September after initially attempting to play through the injury, missed seven weeks before returning to action in Week 9. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year wasted little time demonstrating his value, generating six quarterback pressures on 27 pass-rush attempts, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. He also managed a 22.2% pressure rate while playing 35 of the Rams’ 58 defensive snaps. He also brought his career sack total to 128.5, tying Hall of Famer Jared Allen for the second-most sacks by a player through his first 10 NFL seasons since the statistic became official in 1982. The contest also was the first time Garrett shared the field with Donald , who retired in March 2024. Across 23 plays with both defensive stars on the field, the Rams surrendered just 5.0 yards per play and recorded four sacks. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are signing QB Joey Aguilar off the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad and onto their active roster, according to Jeremy Fowler. This addition at quarterback for the Cardinals comes after the team traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens and with Gardner Minshew "likely" needing season-ending surgery on a torn UCL, per Adam Schefter . Already on the roster at quarterback for the Cardinals are Carson Beck and Josh Johnson, whom Arizona signed off the Bengals ' practice squad on Monday. Aguilar signed with the Jaguars following the 2026 NFL draft as an undrafted rookie. He appeared in all three preseason games, completing 17-of-20 passes for 230 yards with a touchdown pass. After being released during roster cutdowns, the Jaguars brought Aguilar back on the practice squad. Throughout offseason programs and training camp, Liam Coen liked what he saw from Aguilar and wanted to continue working with him. On the 53-man roster at QB for the Jaguars are Trevor Lawrence and Quinn Ewers. Nick Mullens remains on the practice squad. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. The 49ers followed those wins with a 42-10 rout in 2023 and a 30-24 victory in the most recent meeting on Oct. 27, 2024. CB Upton Stout (shoulder, neck), DB Siran Neal (knee, foot), Hobbs (adductor), and Robinson (ankle) are questionable. Hobbs and Robinson returned to practice this week after the 49ers opened their respective practice windows on Wednesday. Both players were limited in all practices throughout the week. Robinson's potential return this Sunday would provide reinforcements as the 49ers are navigating injuries along the receiver front. Robinson has been sidelined since Week 2 after suffering an ankle injury during the game vs the Miami Dolphins. Neal returned to a limited practice on Friday after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday with knee and foot injuries. Stout was limited throughout the week with a shoulder injury and was also listed with a neck injury Friday. The 49ers will be without three wide receivers Sunday, with Evans, Kirk, and Samuel Sr., all ruled out. Bosa was limited on Wednesday and Thursday with knee and calf injuries before practicing in full on Friday. The defensive lineman has been sidelined since Week 2 and is now cleared to return against Las Vegas. McCaffrey also made progress throughout the week after dealing with a hamstring strain that happened during the team's Week 7 game in Atlanta. The running back sat out Wednesday, was limited on Thursday, and a full participant Friday. LB Luke Gifford (groin), S Marques Sigle (ankle), and LB Garret Wallow (hamstring) were limited on Wednesday and Thursday before returning to full on Friday. All three carry no game designations after missing the team's Week 7 matchup. The 49ers return to Levi's® Stadium with a 6-1 record following their Week 8 Bye, looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season against Atlanta. away.headline: 49ers Receive Sobering Injury Update on Mike Evans
away.blurb: He hasn't played since he hobbled off the field at Levi's Stadium with an Achilles injury on Oct. 19. He won't play today when the 49ers face the Las Vegas Raiders at home. And he's "questionable at best" to play next week when the 49ers face the Dallas Cowboys on the road, according to Mike Garafolo. Still, Evans is 33. McCaffrey was 28 in 2024, and he missed the first eight games of the season, then he had a Week 9 bye week to help him get ready for his Week 10 season debut. That's how long it took him to get ready to play. He even had to fly to Germany to receive treatment that isn't available in the United States. And when he came back, he lasted only four games before he suffered a season-ending injury in his knee, which might have been a compensation injury that was related to his Achilles. Now, the 49ers are coming off a bye week. Shanahan has had plenty of time to figure out how to move the ball and score points without Evans. 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan Explains Plan for Mike Evans' Return 49ers Rule Out 3 Key Players for Week 9 vs. Raiders 49ers Receive Sobering Injury Update on Mike Evans Skip to main content SI.COM Don't expect to see Mike Evans on the field any time soon. "He's dealing with some tendinitis," Garafolo said . "We know how painful that can be...He is improving. He is working his way back. But Christian McCaffrey dealt with this a couple years ago, so the 49ers know how painful and debilitating it can be." It's interesting that Garafolo compared Mike Evans' injury to the tendinitis McCaffrey suffered two seasons ago. Granted, McCaffrey had bilateral Achilles tendinitis, meaning he had it in both legs. Evans has it in just one. If the 49ers learned their lesson with McCaffrey, they should let Evans take as long as he needs to recover completely before letting him play again. If that means sitting him until Week 14 or 15 or later, so be it. Because if he returns too soon and goes down again, the 49ers won't win the Super Bowl. But if he's 100 percent healthy when the playoffs start, they absolutely could win it all. He's that important. Which means the next couple weeks or couple months could depend on Kyle Shanahan's ability to trust his young players on offense. We know he prefers playing guys in their 30s. We know he has no patience for young players when they make the smallest mistakes. He has to find some patience. He has two terrific young weapons in Jordan Watkins and Kaelon Black. Use them. If Shanahan had trusted them and used them more two weeks ago, they would have beaten the Falcons. Instead, Shanahan overused McCaffrey on the first drive and he got injured. Then Shanahan kept calling plays for Christian Kirk and Brandon Cooks, both of whom are washed. Let's see what Shanahan cooked up. home.headline: Week 9 injury report: Colts could catch a break against Cowboys
home.blurb: Jonathan Taylor, Keenan Allen, and Charvarius Ward all returned to full participation after sitting out Wednesday on rest days. None of the three absences appears particularly concerning, and all should be in a good position to play Sunday barring an unexpected setback. Indianapolis could also receive reinforcements at a couple of positions. Linebacker Bryce Boettcher and wide receiver Anthony Gould have both logged consecutive full practices after missing the previous two games. Gould is still required to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before returning to game action, but his progress is an encouraging sign. Boettcher's potential return would be particularly helpful for a linebacker group dealing with some uncertainty. Tight end Drew Ogletree also showed some progress, moving from a DNP designation Wednesday to limited participation Thursday. His availability remains unclear, but the progression is a positive development. The Cowboys could receive some reinforcements at linebacker, with Dee Winters progressing from limited participation Wednesday to a full practice Thursday. Winters' potential return would be particularly helpful with DeMarvion Overshown being limited with hamstring and back issues. Meanwhile, Marist Liufau has also returned to full participation as he works through his 21-day return-to-practice window, potentially giving Dallas another option at linebacker. The secondary is another area worth monitoring. Caleb Downs and P.J. Locke both progressed from not participating Wednesday to limited participation Thursday while dealing with concussions, an encouraging sign for Dallas. Both players must complete the NFL's concussion return-to-participation protocol. Their return to practice is encouraging, but neither is guaranteed to be available Sunday. Joey Porter Jr. also went from a full participant on Wednesday to limited on Thursday with an ankle injury. With multiple defensive backs dealing with injuries, Dallas could be facing some significant depth concerns against Indianapolis. At tight end, Jake Ferguson has missed the first two practices of the week with an ankle injury, leaving his availability for Sunday in question. Luke Schoonmaker has been limited in consecutive practices while dealing with a groin injury, but his participation is an encouraging sign. Getting Schoonmaker back would be particularly important if Ferguson remains sidelined, as Dallas could otherwise be severely shorthanded. The Cowboys also have some questions at wide receiver, where George Pickens has been limited for two consecutive days with a hamstring injury. His continued participation is encouraging, but his status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday. KaVontae Turpin, meanwhile, has missed both practices with a rib injury. His potential absence would affect both the receiving corps and special teams, where he provides an explosive return option. home.headline: Cowboys Offer Worrisome Injury Update Ahead Of Crucial 49ers Showdown
home.blurb: With the San Francisco 49ers up next, the Cowboys need everyone available to even have a shot at what would be an upset win in Week 10. "Busy week in the training room for us," Schottenheimer said. "PJ Locke will not be available this week. Jake Ferguson and Tyler Goodson should both miss multiple weeks. We're working through that. "[Donovan] Ezeiruaku, he's got an ankle sprain. See how he does. [Jonathan] Mingo, [KaVontae] Turpin, GP [Pickens], and JPJ [Joey Porter] try to get them back out there this week working, and see how they do. It was a busy day in the training room." Then Pickens and Porter Jr. appear, at least right now, to be questionable, while it isn't known if linebacker DeMarvion Overshown will be available, although he did look in good condition running onto the field to celebrate a Shemar James fumble recovery, which Schottenheimer called "unacceptable." Already in a hole, Dallas, while at home, will be up against it as Kyle Shanahan's team has made a habit of making an example out of the Cowboys over the years. The hope is that as the week goes on, it'll start to clear out. home.headline: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
home.blurb: Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games. Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role. Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives Skip to main content SI.COM Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons. The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson. The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52. The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule. "I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far." "We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based." Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning. “It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here. "I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday." The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football. away.headline: Ravens lose kicker Jake Moody to Falcons, must find replacement before Chargers game
away.blurb: The former third-round draft pick out of Michigan was subsequently returned to Baltimore's practice squad before being claimed by Atlanta. November 10, 2026 / 4:51 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons reportedly poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody is signing with the Falcons and will be added to their 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

home.headline: Desperate Baltimore Ravens seal huge NFL quarterback trade after Jackson and Huntley injuries
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens have found a fix to their quarterback injury woes by trading for Arizona Cardinals star Jacoby Brissett. The Ravens are down to third-choice undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano ahead of Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , leaving general manager Eric DaCosta desperately scrabbling around for a long-term solution. NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report on Wednesday that the Ravens are now finalizing a trade for Brissett, with the deal set to be completed over the weekend. Fagnano will therefore be on the field for Baltimore on Thursday night, before Brissett takes the quarterback reins in Week 10 for the Monday Night Football showdown against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett had become a prime trade candidate in Arizona after being benched midgame against the Dallas Cowboys and then dropped to QB3 on the depth chart. He started the first eight games of the season for Arizona this season, going 3-5 with a 63.3% pass completion. After Brissett was benched during the loss to the Cowboys, the starting job was handed to Gardner Minshew, with Carson Beck the backup. West Palm Beach native Brissett will join his seventh NFL team in Baltimore, in his 11th season in the league. He was first selected by the New England Patriots in the third round of the 2016 Draft, going on to win the Super Bowl as Tom Brady's backup in his first season. He was traded to the Colts after his rookie season and was the starter there in 2017 and 2019, before alternating as a back-up and starter in Miami, Cleveland, Washington and back in New England, before eventually landing in Arizona. In March 2025 he signed a two-year, $12.5 million deal with the Cardinals and played in 14 games last season. Despite reworking his contract to increase his compensation for the 2026 season, he will become a free agent at the end of the campaign, unless he agrees new terms in Baltimore.

home.headline: Ravens lose kicker Jake Moody to Falcons, must find replacement before Chargers game
home.blurb: The former third-round draft pick out of Michigan was subsequently returned to Baltimore's practice squad before being claimed by Atlanta. November 10, 2026 / 4:51 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons reportedly poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody is signing with the Falcons and will be added to their 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.
